children: The midpoint of Flight Centre's FY 2027 profit guidance at roughly 308 million Australian dollars is largely in line with Visible Alpha consensus of A$311 million, Citi notes. The guidance "effectively implies no market growth" year over year, the bank says. It also assumes no disruption in 4Q FY 2027 and that the travel agency "realizes a somewhat normal Leisure and Touring quarter," Citi says. At present, that appears a reasonable assumption, with consumer and corporate demand appearing somewhat resilient to high airline prices, says the bank. "However, we expect the outlook to constantly change with the various factors at play," it says. Citi has a neutral rating on Flight Centre, with a share-price target of A$13.20. The stock is down 0.6% at A$12.515. (rhiannon.hoyle@wsj.com; @RhiannonHoyle)
